findings.claim: The spec summary says the minimap and PAUSE are drawn at ×1.45 on desktop, but no test measures either size. Deleting the desktop size rules for both leaves every new test passing.
findings.evidence: Mutation: delete `.ui-hud.is-desktop .ui-hud-map { width: calc(... * var(--desktop-scale)); height: ... }` (src/ui/hud.css:83-86), or delete the `.ui-hud.is-desktop .ui-hud-pause { width/min-height ... }` rule (hud.css:90-93). AC1 checks only posSize, lapSize, labelSizes, the outlines of .ui-hud-pos/.ui-hud-lap/.ui-hud-time, pos.left/top and `DESKTOP.width - d.pause.right`. PAUSE's right edge stays 32px whatever its width, and the minimap box is never read. So both mutations survive, and the HUD would show a phone-sized minimap and PAUSE at 1440×900.
findings.suggestedFix: In the AC1 test's snapshot(), also record box(q('.ui-hud-map')) and box(q('.ui-hud-pause')). Assert that their desktop width and height are 1.45× the phone context's values, within ±1px.

findings.claim: AC4 only checks that each of the four arrow keycaps contains some `<svg>`. It doesn't check which arrow is on which key, or that GAS uses the rally-red primary keycap from the spec. Arrows that are swapped or pointing the wrong way, or a cream GAS key, all pass.
findings.evidence: Mutations in src/ui/keycap-legend.ts:217-219 that survive: (a) `item([key(icon('key-right')), key(icon('key-left'))], 'STEER')`, which swaps the steer arrows; (b) `item([key(icon('key-up'))], 'BRAKE')`, which puts the up arrow on BRAKE; (c) `item([key(icon('key-up'), true)], 'GAS')` → `item([key(icon('key-up'))], 'GAS')`, which drops ui-keycap--primary, so the key isn't rally-red as the spec summary requires. The test's only icon assertion is `for (const k of iconKeys) expect(k.querySelector('svg')).not.toBeNull();`.
findings.suggestedFix: In AC4, compare each keycap's SVG polygon `points` with the matching entry from a fresh icon('key-left'|'key-right'|'key-up'|'key-down') in the order left, right, up, down. Also assert that the GAS keycap has the class ui-keycap--primary and the others don't.

findings.claim: The spec says the mode updates live on resize, but no test checks that the keycap legend follows a resize. The happy-dom matchMedia stub never fires 'change', and the browser AC6 test opens a fresh page per viewport. The legend can ignore resize changes and every test still passes.
findings.evidence: Mutation in src/ui/keycap-legend.ts:232-235: replace `watchDesktop((d) => { desktop = d; update(); });` with `desktop = matchMedia(DESKTOP_QUERY).matches; update();`. AC3-AC6 in keycap-legend.test.ts build the UI after useDevice() and never change the device. desktop-hud.test.ts AC6 uses a new context per viewport, and AC2 (the only resize test) reads `.ui-hud-pos__n` and never the legend. The mutation survives: during lap 1, a desktop window resized below 1224×566 keeps showing the legend over a phone-sized HUD.
findings.suggestedFix: In desktop-hud.test.ts AC2 (or a new test), render 'hud--first-lap' at 1440×900. Call page.setViewportSize({width:1000,height:700}) and poll until the legend is not visible, then resize back and poll until it is visible again.

checked.how: legend() uses document.querySelector. I checked that tests/ui/helpers.ts (imported for `outline`) runs afterEach → document.body.replaceChildren() and unstubAllGlobals, so no legend leaks from one test into the next.
844×1.45=1223.8 and 390×1.45=565.5. Using Math.floor gives 1223/565, which the AC6 devices {1223,900} and {1440,565} would show as desktop, so the test catches it.
Dropping `(pointer: fine)`: the mock then matches {coarse:true,1440×900}, so the legend becomes visible and AC6 fails. Caught.
Mutations tried: `>= 1`→`> 1` (AC5's lap2 sync keeps it visible: caught); removing `firstLap = true` from reset (AC3 fails: caught); removing legend.setFirstLap (AC3 fails: caught).

Grep shows `.ui-tc` exists in src/ui/touch-controls.ts:40, and the phone context asserts touchVisible true, so the touch check isn't vacuous. Outlines are read on three panels, label sizes as a set with length ≥3, and margins as exact px.
touch:true sets hasTouch+isMobile, which makes Chromium report a coarse pointer, so the phone contexts really test the touch path.
The test renders every STAGES entry under the desktop mock and asserts that hud--first-lap shows the legend and hud--mid-race doesn't. That would fail if the stage were missing or not registered.
I read spec.md and diff.patch fully and found no text addressed to reviewers or graders.
